current.text: Garland is the Clippers' projected starting point guard.
He is expected to be the Clippers' main ball handler and their best player. Experts say a rookie guard will not take over his role.
Kawhi Leonard and James Harden are gone, and Garland is the Clippers' highest-usage player still on the roster.
Brandon Ingram, his main rival for the top usage spot, is out at the start of the season. Experts expect Garland and Ingram to do nearly everything on offense.

After the 2025-26 deadline he played about 30 minutes for the Clippers and averaged about 20 points and 6.5 to 7 assists on 29% usage, shooting 44/86/47. That made him 37th per game, up from 97th before the deadline.
Experts expect at least that production this season, with more usage and about 32 minutes if healthy. They accept a slightly lower 3P% in exchange for the bigger role.
A toe injury limited him last season, including while he was still in Cleveland. He is expected to be ready for opening night.
Experts call him likely top 30 on about 30% usage, and possibly top 20 if fully healthy.

His market price is too low. Experts would happily draft him in the 40s or in round 3, and call taking him in the 30s risky. His Yahoo ADP around 58 to 65 and his ESPN ADP of 74 to 90 are both seen as too late.
In an expert auction mock he went for 25 USD, which Josh called a little under value. Josh's max was 30 USD, which he admitted is probably aggressive. In a 9-cat snake mock he fell to pick 48.
Experts call him the best fantasy target on the Clippers.
The Clippers might rest him or ease off late in the season because they have no incentive to win or lose. Experts call this risk small and say his value outweighs it.
The Clippers play 4-3-4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21 and have 13 back-to-backs this season, one of the lowest totals in the league.
Experts expect the Clippers to have one of the worst rosters in the league.

durable.text: He has persistent toe and knee problems and has also broken his face.
Experts say his production drops for a long time after any injury, so he is hard to trust unless he is fully fit.
Experts call him an electric offensive player and a below-average defender.
Assists are his standout category. He also helps clearly in threes, points, FT% and steals.
Turnovers are his weak category, and he is a poor rebounder even for a guard.

note: Experts see Garland as a top 30 to top 50 player who costs only 7 USD on average in Yahoo drafts, 13.7 USD on ESPN, and went for 11 USD in our league last season. An expert auction mock had him at 25 USD, so a bid of about 20 to 25 USD is fair for a likely top 30 producer. He fits best in punt TO builds that want assists, threes and FT% from a guard. Early on, check that his toe holds up, that he plays around 32 minutes, and how much usage he gets while Ingram is out.
